```{r Loading libraries, include=FALSE}
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(ismev)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r loading data, include=FALSE}
# Extend R's default HTTP timeout limit to 300 seconds
options(timeout = 300)

cache_file <- "river_don_parkhill_flow.rds"

if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
  # Load from local cache if file already exists
  river_data <- readRDS(cache_file)
  
} else {
  # If no local cache exists, fetch from SEPA in 1-year chunks
  start_years <- seq(2016, 2025, by = 1)
  
  fetch_chunk <- function(yr) {
    from_date <- paste0(yr, "-08-31T00:00:00")
    to_date   <- paste0(yr + 1, "-08-31T00:00:00")
    
    url <- paste0(
      "https://timeseries.sepa.org.uk/KiWIS/KiWIS?",
      "service=kisters&type=queryServices&datasource=0&",
      "request=getTimeseriesValues&ts_path=1/234292/Q/15m.Cmd&",
      "from=", from_date, "&to=", to_date, "&",
      "metadata=true&returnfields=Timestamp,Value,Quality%20Code&format=csv"
    )
    
    read_delim(
      url, 
      delim = ";", 
      comment = "#",
      col_names = c("Timestamp", "Discharge", "QualityCode"),
      show_col_types = FALSE
    )
  }
  
  river_data <- map_dfr(start_years, fetch_chunk) %>%
    mutate(Timestamp = as.POSIXct(Timestamp, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Discharge)) %>%
    distinct(Timestamp, .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  # Save to local file so future runs don't need to use the API
  saveRDS(river_data, cache_file)
}
```

## Filtering and Cleaning

```{r tidying the data, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
quality_code_table <- tibble(
  `Code number` = c(50, 100, 140, 150, 200, 254),
  `Code name` = c(
    "Good",
    "Estimated",
    "Provisional",
    "Suspect",
    "Unchecked (imported from legacy database)",
    "Unchecked"
  ),
  `Abbreviated code name` = c("G", "E", "Prov", "S", "V", "U")
)

quality_combined <- quality_code_table %>%
  left_join(
    river_data %>%
      mutate(QualityCode = as.numeric(QualityCode)) %>%
      count(QualityCode, name = "Count"),
    by = c("Code number" = "QualityCode")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Count = coalesce(Count, 0L),
    Percentage = sprintf("%.2f%%", Count / sum(Count) * 100)
  )

quality_combined %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Table 1 — quality codes and their frequency in the data",
    align = c("c", "l", "c", "r", "r"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("bordered", "striped", "hover"),
    full_width = FALSE)
```

- Justify why kept 100 and above but not 254

## Exploratory Analysis

Throughout the report, we add three time variables to support our analysis: the month, the season, and the water year. The water year runs from September to August and is labelled by the year it ends in, which keeps each winter's high flows together in the same year.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
river_data <- river_data %>%
  mutate(
    month      = month(Timestamp, label = TRUE),
    water_year = if_else(month(Timestamp) >= 9, year(Timestamp) + 1, year(Timestamp)),
    season     = case_when(
      month(Timestamp) %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
      month(Timestamp) %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring",
      month(Timestamp) %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer",
      TRUE                              ~ "Autumn"
    ),
    season = factor(season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn"))
  )
```

### Main time series and summary table

We first construct the hydrograph for Don at Parkhill over our chosen period.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
ggplot(river_data, aes(x = Timestamp, y = Discharge)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Hydrograph: Don at Parkhill (15-min Interval)",
    subtitle = "August 2016 – August 2026",
    x = "Date",
    y = expression("Discharge ("*m^3*"/s)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
river_data %>%
  summarise(
    `Mean`               = mean(Discharge),
    `Standard deviation` = sd(Discharge),
    `Minimum`            = min(Discharge),
    `25th percentile`    = quantile(Discharge, 0.25),
    `Median`             = median(Discharge),
    `75th percentile`    = quantile(Discharge, 0.75),
    `95th percentile`    = quantile(Discharge, 0.95),
    `99th percentile`    = quantile(Discharge, 0.99),
    `Maximum`            = max(Discharge)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Statistic", values_to = "Value") %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Summary statistics for 15-minute discharge (m³/s)") %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("bordered", "striped", "hover"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(river_data, aes(x = Discharge)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = quantile(river_data$Discharge, c(0.5, 0.95, 0.99)),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of 15-minute discharge",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines: median, 95th and 99th percentiles (log scale)",
    x = expression("Discharge ("*m^3*"/s)"),
    y = "Number of readings"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

We observe that discharge is low for most of the year, with a smaller number of large peaks. The strong-right skew of the distribution confirms this, with a median discharge of 14.91 $m^3/s$, and a 99th percentile of 130.96 $m^3/s$. 

### Yearly trends 

From figure ..., we also observe an upward trend in discharge, and larger maximum flows, over the time period.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
river_data %>%
  group_by(water_year) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean    = mean(Discharge),
    Median  = median(Discharge),
    Maximum = max(Discharge),
    `Date of maximum` = format(Timestamp[which.max(Discharge)], "%d %b %Y")

  rename(`Water year` = water_year) %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Discharge by water year (m³/s)") %>%

yearly <- river_data %>%

```

### Exploring seasonal trends overall

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Mean discharge for each month
monthly <- river_data %>%
  mutate(month_num = as.numeric(format(Timestamp, "%m"))) %>%
  group_by(month_num) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(Discharge)) %>%
  mutate(
    month  = month.abb[month_num],
    season = case_when(
      month_num %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Autumn",
      month_num %in% c(12, 1, 2)  ~ "Winter",
      month_num %in% c(3, 4, 5)   ~ "Spring",
      TRUE                        ~ "Summer"
    ),
    season = factor(season, levels = c("Autumn", "Winter", "Spring", "Summer")),
    month_order = (month_num - 9) %% 12   # Sep = 0, Oct = 1, ..., Aug = 11
  ) %>%
  arrange(month_order)
monthly$id <- 1:nrow(monthly)

# Angle and alignment of each month label
monthly$angle <- 90 - 360 * (monthly$id - 0.5) / nrow(monthly)
monthly$hjust <- ifelse(monthly$angle < -90, 1, 0)
monthly$angle <- ifelse(monthly$angle < -90, monthly$angle + 180, monthly$angle)

# Line under each season and position of its name
base_data <- monthly %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(start = min(id), end = max(id)) %>%
  mutate(title = (start + end) / 2)

# Grid lines every 10 up to 40
grid_breaks <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)
y_max <- max(c(monthly$value, 40))

ggplot(monthly, aes(x = as.factor(id), y = value, fill = season)) +
  geom_blank() +   # sets up the discrete x-axis before the grid labels
  geom_col(alpha = 0.6, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = grid_breaks, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = grid_breaks, label = grid_breaks,
           colour = "grey30", size = 3, fontface = "bold", vjust = -0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Autumn" = "#F28E2B", "Winter" = "#4E79A7",
                               "Spring" = "#59A14F", "Summer" = "#EDC948")) +
  ylim(-y_max, y_max * 1.4) +
  coord_polar() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = unit(rep(-1, 4), "cm")
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(x = id, y = value + y_max * 0.05, label = month,
                hjust = hjust, angle = angle),
            colour = "black", alpha = 0.7, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_segment(data = base_data,
               aes(x = start - 0.4, y = -y_max * 0.05, xend = end + 0.4, yend = -y_max * 0.05),
               colour = "black", alpha = 0.8, linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = base_data,
            aes(x = title, y = -y_max * 0.41, label = season),
            colour = "black", alpha = 0.8, size = 4, fontface = "bold",
            inherit.aes = FALSE)
```

season_colours <- c("Autumn" = "#F28E2B", "Winter" = "#4E79A7",

```

ggplot(seasonal, aes(x = factor(water_year), y = Mean, colour = season, group = season)) +

    title = "Mean discharge by season in each water year",

    y = expression("Mean discharge ("*m^3*"/s)"),
    colour = "Season"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(seasonal, aes(x = factor(water_year), y = Maximum, colour = season, group = season)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = season_colours) +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum discharge by season in each water year",
    x = "Water year ending",
    y = expression("Maximum discharge ("*m^3*"/s)"),
    colour = "Season"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Threshold Selection
The Peaks-Over-Threshold (POT) uses a threshold to extracts the distinct peak flows for extreme events. The threshold is typically selected from three main methods: 

  1.	3-5 per year method
  2.	95th Percentile method
  3.	Mean residual life threshold analysis
  
```{r plots, echo=FALSE, fig.pos='h', fig.width=10, fig.height=10}
plot_35 / plot_95 / plot_gpd 
```

The figures above are a comparison of the thresholds selected by each method. Prior to independence analysis, a practical approach is to choose an initial threshold that is likely to be too low, i.e. $(u = 65)$. This means when the distinct extreme events are selected, all the major peaks are being analysed, and subsequentially the threshold can be raised.
